correspondence.scope: Western headwater approach and southern reservoir bend
correspondence.finding: The selected upper approach runs east and southeast through the mapped San Francisco drainage toward Presa Gobernador Leobardo Reynoso (Trujillo), then turns east and north into the Aguanaval corridor west of Fresnillo. The municipal relief sheet separates San Francisco from Río Aguanaval; the state watercourse map identifies the reservoir between them. The extreme starting feeder and precise name/reservoir transition vertices are not assigned. The reservoir passage is not treated as a continuous natural river channel.

The route's northward reach, westward bend through the El Cazadero setting, passage by Río Grande and subsequent north/northeast continuation agree with the state map's Aguanaval course. Its accompanying basin sheet places this corridor in the Aguanaval drainage, distinct from the closed eastern El Salado units. Río Grande is used here as a mapped settlement anchor; it is not adopted as an alias solely from the adjacent town label.

correspondence.scope: Eastern Durango and southwestern Coahuila middle course
correspondence.finding: The broad eastern bulge, west/northwest turn and northward confined course follow the river repeatedly labeled Aguanaval on the adjoining Durango and Coahuila sheets. Durango's map shows the Santiago–Santa Clara tributary approaching separately from the southwest, and distinguishes Arroyo de Cuencamé and Nazas farther west. These river shapes and junction relationships support Aguanaval for the long middle corridor without assigning the joining tributary's name to the selected line.

correspondence.scope: Lower northward connector and eastern receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: South and east of Torreón, the selected route leaves the north/east-trending named Aguanaval approach and follows a further northward connector before bending east. The Coahuila watercourse map marks that connector with the dot-bearing canal symbol from its legend, distinguishing it from the ordinary river symbol. Viesca's relief sheet shows the corresponding eastern drainage network and a separate Arroyo La Barranca label. The evidence does not establish every connector or receiving-channel vertex as naturally and uniformly named Aguanaval, nor justify transferring La Barranca to the entire lower reach.

correspondence.scope: Viesca terminal lowland and feature-class limit
correspondence.finding: The final east/southeast continuation reaches the lowland northeast of Viesca, where the municipal map depicts several branching and rectilinear drainage lines. Its hydrology table distinguishes the Aguanaval subbasins from the Laguna de Viesca subbasin. These sources support terminal-basin context, not an exact natural mouth, a presently inundated lake or uninterrupted flow along the model. The separate Nazas course toward the San Pedro/Mayrán setting is shown farther north on the state map.

The southern hook and succeeding northwestward leg occupy the Hamlin Valley setting along the Utah–Nevada border before approaching southern Snake Valley. The state location map distinguishes Hamlin from Pine Valley farther east. The separate Area 19 description names Hamlin Valley Wash and says the valley opens northward into Snake Valley. This supports local drainage context, without naming the initial feeder or every selected southern segment.

The route turns northeast and then north through the Garrison–Eskdale latitude belt into Snake Valley, between the Snake Range and Confusion Range settings. The UGS map depicts Lake Creek, Snake Creek, Baker Creek, Warm Creek, springs and groundwater-discharge areas separately. Their positions support the basin correspondence; none supplies a continuous name for the selected valley-floor line. In particular, Snake Valley is not evidence for a river named Snake River.

The selected line continues north, then northeast toward the Callao–Fish Springs regional setting and onto the southern Great Salt Lake Desert. The basin map places Callao at the northern Snake Valley margin and distinguishes the Fish Springs Range and refuge to the east. The selection does not thereby become Fish Springs or a tributary named for that refuge.

correspondence.scope: Long desert and western lake approach
correspondence.finding: Beyond the valley, the route makes its extended northward and eastward desert bends and continues toward the western lake margin near the Lakeside setting. The state map distinguishes the Great Salt Lake Desert, Newfoundland Evaporation Basin and Great Salt Lake. Its hydrology discussion describes temporary ponding and no perennial stream reaching the lake from this basin. The modeled continuity therefore does not establish a single present flowing river; neither small fragment joins nor the long desert continuation establish named-channel boundaries.

The northernmost piece proceeds toward the Lakeside/railroad-causeway setting and then north and northeast into western Gunnison Bay. The retained UGS overview separates the lake, evaporation ponds, causeway, islands and surrounding mountains. It supports terminal-waterbody context, not an onward river hydronym. Its contrasting historical-average and 2022-low shorelines also preclude treating the selected line as a fixed current shoreline or river mouth. Bear River is separately shown entering the lake from the east.

correspondence: The complete single selected fragment was inspected: an initially southward interior leg, a southeastward low bend, a long undulating east-northeast middle section, a stepped southeastern descent, and a final east-northeast approach. No additional tributary fragment is present.

The long western and central corridor crosses mapped Inland Ice. The eastern approach reaches the more broken ice-margin and land/fjord setting inland of the Scoresby Sund region. The original graticule and regional ice/land pattern support this feature-class distinction without assigning a precise terminal glacier, stream or fjord.

No natural river name is established for the complete modeled line by the readable original. A nearby glacier, land or fjord label is not evidence that the whole interior-to-margin path is a uniformly named river, nor that it represents known subglacial connectivity.

The mapped ice-surface contours, thickness isopachs and bedrock contours describe ice and terrain rather than named river channels. Historical mapping does not establish a current ice-front position, present flow direction or an active surface-water connection along this model path.

correspondence.finding: The southeastern start descends through the Senneville–Blouin setting, then turns west toward the Harricana outlet corridor. OBVAJ’s hydrography and detailed southern sheet distinguish this selected approach from the Bourlamaque and Milky contributions. The model does not trace all of the Mourier–Lemoine–De Montigny source-lake chain.

The route then passes through the Malartic and La Motte lake corridor and the Figuery setting before continuing through Amos. These separate lake waterbodies interrupt any simple whole-line river-name interpretation, while their sequence strongly identifies the Harricana route.

North of Amos, the selected trunk continues past the Obalski setting and along the north-to-northwest Harricana course. The CEHQ sheet shows this corridor separately from the Bell–Nottaway drainage to the east and the Abitibi drainage to the west. It remains on the main Harricana corridor at the western branch junction.

All three non-mainstem pieces form a single contributing approach: the western piece runs north, the middle piece turns east, and the short eastern piece reaches the Harricana. Their connected shape and position match the lower Rivière Turgeon on the CEHQ map. Turgeon is a tributary name, not an alias of Harricana; the selection does not include its complete upstream basin.

Beyond the branch junction, the northern piece continues northwest along the lower Harricana toward the southern James Bay coastal setting and across the provincial boundary. The provincial conservation plan independently describes the river crossing into Ontario before reaching James Bay. The selection is treated as a terminal river-mouth approach, without assigning a surveyed mouth, tidal limit or the wider estuary to this line.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
